terms.title: Tally Terms of Use
terms.summary: Tally writes bedtime stories with artificial intelligence (AI). Stories are new every time and aren't checked by a person before you see them, so please read them with your child. By tapping "I agree" you accept these terms.

sections.heading: 1. About these terms
paragraphs: These terms are an agreement between you and the provider of Tally, Yaron Ogen, Humboldtstr. 12, 06114 Halle (Saale), Germany ("we", "us"). They apply whenever you use the Tally app.

Tally is meant for parents and other adults who read stories to children. You must be at least 18 years old (or the age of majority where you live) to use it. Children can listen and join in, but an adult sets up and manages the app.

sections.heading: 2. Stories are created by artificial intelligence
paragraphs: Every story, question, answer choice, title and ending in Tally is generated by AI language models provided by third parties (currently OpenAI). They are written automatically for your request and are not written or checked by a person before you read them.

We instruct the AI to write warm, calm and age-appropriate stories, and we check every story automatically for language, length and safety rules. Even so, AI can make mistakes: a story may contain errors, odd or repetitive passages, facts that aren't true, or, rarely, something you find unsuitable for your child.
Please read or listen to each story yourself, and use your own judgement before or while sharing it with your child. You can stop, skip or delete any story at any time.

Premium plans add a picture to every story. Pictures are also created by AI (an image model from OpenAI) in Tally's own illustration style, without your child's name or any personal details, and are checked automatically for safety.
Stories are for entertainment only. They are not educational, medical, psychological or other professional advice. Any similarity to existing books, characters or real people is unintended.

sections.heading: 3. Information you give us
paragraphs: To personalise stories you can give us your child's first name and age, and whether stories should call your child a girl or a boy. Only give information you are allowed to share.
Your child's name is never sent to the AI: stories are written with a placeholder, and the name is added on our servers. Names are stored encrypted.
If you describe a main character of your own, that description is sent to the AI to write the story. Don't include real names or personal details of anyone in it.

When you rate a story, the score is stored together with how the story was made (for example its language, length and themes) so we can improve Tally. These statistics are anonymous and are never shown to other users.
Our Privacy Policy (https://tallyapi-production-1103.up.railway.app/privacy, also linked in the app under Settings) explains in detail what we collect, why, how long we keep it, and your rights.

sections.heading: 4. Using Tally fairly
paragraphs: Please don't try to make the AI produce harmful, hateful, sexual or violent content, don't enter other people's personal information, don't try to get around usage limits, and don't copy, resell or attack the app or its servers.
We may limit or close accounts that break these rules.

sections.heading: 5. Subscriptions
paragraphs: Without a subscription you can read Tally's sample stories. Creating stories needs a subscription: Premium or Premium Plus, monthly plans with 30 or 60 stories a month (a Choose what happens story counts as 2), pictures, choices, Books and PDFs, as described in the app at the time you subscribe. If your subscription ends, you can still read the stories you already made, but you can't create new ones until you subscribe again.

Subscriptions are sold by Apple (App Store) or Google (Google Play) and renew automatically until you cancel. You can cancel in your store account settings at least 24 hours before the renewal date. Payments, refunds and cancellations are handled by the store under its terms. Deleting your account doesn't cancel a store subscription.
Monthly story allowances don't carry over to the next month.

sections.heading: 6. Your stories
paragraphs: You may read, print, save and share the stories created for you with family and friends, for personal, non-commercial use. As far as the law allows, we don't claim ownership of your stories, but please be aware that AI-generated text may not be protected by copyright.
The Tally app, its design, illustrations and name remain ours.

sections.heading: 7. Availability and changes
paragraphs: We work to keep Tally running smoothly but can't promise that it will always be available or error-free. We may change, add or remove features.
You can delete your account at any time in Settings. This deletes your children's profiles and stories.
If we change these terms in an important way, we'll ask you to agree again in the app.

sections.heading: 8. Responsibility
paragraphs: We are liable without limitation for damage we cause intentionally or through gross negligence, for injury to life, body or health, and wherever mandatory law (such as the German Product Liability Act) provides for it.

For slight negligence, we are liable only if we breach an obligation that is essential for using Tally as agreed, and then only for the typical damage that could be foreseen. Otherwise we are not liable for slight negligence.

Stories and pictures are written and drawn by AI and are not checked by a person (section 2). Please read each story yourself before or while sharing it with your child, and report any story that seems wrong (the report option is under every story).
Nothing in these terms limits rights you have under consumer-protection law that can't be excluded.

sections.heading: 9. Contact
paragraphs: Tally is provided by Yaron Ogen, Humboldtstr. 12, 06114 Halle (Saale), Germany. Email: deneb.algedi2026@gmail.com. Legal notice: https://tallyapi-production-1103.up.railway.app/imprint.
These terms are governed by the laws of Germany. If you are a consumer, you also keep the protection of the mandatory laws of the country where you live.
We are neither obliged nor willing to take part in dispute resolution proceedings before a consumer arbitration board.

privacy.title: Tally Privacy Policy
privacy.summary: Tally collects only what it needs to write bedtime stories for your child. Your child's name is never sent to the AI and is stored encrypted, there are no ads and no tracking, and we never sell data. You can delete everything at any time in the app.

sections.heading: 1. Who is responsible
paragraphs: Tally is provided by Yaron Ogen, Humboldtstr. 12, 06114 Halle (Saale), Germany, who is the controller responsible for your data under the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Contact: deneb.algedi2026@gmail.com.
Tally is meant for parents and other adults. Children listen to the stories, but an adult sets up and manages the app.

sections.heading: 2. What we collect
paragraphs: Account: your email address and password (the password is stored only in hashed form by our sign-in provider).

Your child's profile, as you enter it: first name, age, and whether stories should call your child a girl or a boy (for grammar). The name is stored encrypted. We don't ask for or keep your child's birthday.

Stories: the stories written for you, their settings (language, themes, length, ending, main character), your child's choices and answers in the interactive modes, any main-character description you type, the stories you keep in a child's Book, and the scores you give stories.

Account settings and usage: your time zone, how many stories you have used, which version of the Terms you agreed to and when (including your confirmation that you are 18 or older), and your Premium subscription status.
Reports: if you report a story, we keep your reason, any note you add, and a short excerpt of the story with your child's name removed, so we can review it.
Technical data: when the app talks to our server, the server briefly records technical information such as your IP address and the time of the request, for security and troubleshooting.
We do not collect your location, contacts, photos, advertising identifiers, or any data for advertising. We do not use analytics or tracking tools.

sections.heading: 3. Why we use it (and on what legal basis)
paragraphs: To provide the app you asked for: accounts, children's profiles, writing, storing and reading stories, the Book, book PDFs and coloring pages (contract, Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).
To keep the service safe and working, for example preventing abuse, fixing errors and reviewing reported stories (legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
To improve story quality: story scores are kept as anonymous statistics, together with how the story was made, but without who rated it (legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Your child's details are used only to write stories for your family. We never use them for advertising or profiling.

sections.heading: 4. Artificial intelligence
paragraphs: Stories, questions and answer choices are written by AI models from OpenAI. To write a story, the AI receives only the story settings: language, your child's age, themes, length, ending, grammatical gender, the main-character choice or description you typed, and your child's choices and answers.

The AI never receives your child's name or your email. Stories are written with a placeholder, and the name is filled in on our server afterwards. The same applies to story pictures (Premium plans): the picture AI only receives a description of the scene.
After a story is written, a second AI step checks its grammar and spelling. It receives the same story text (still without your child's name) and nothing else.
OpenAI processes this data on our behalf through its business API, does not use it to train its models, and keeps it only for a short period under its commercial terms.

sections.heading: 5. Service providers
paragraphs: We use carefully chosen providers who process data only on our instructions (data processing agreements, Art. 28 GDPR):
Supabase: sign-in, sign-in emails (confirming your address, resetting your password) and database, hosted in Frankfurt, Germany.
Railway: hosting of our application server.

OpenAI: the AI that writes and proofreads the stories (see section 4). On Premium plans it also draws a picture for each story, and redraws it as outlines when you ask for a coloring page. For pictures it receives only an English description of the scene and characters (or the picture itself), never your child's name or your email.

Apple, Google and RevenueCat: Premium subscriptions are sold and billed by Apple (App Store) or Google (Google Play). RevenueCat tells us whether a subscription is active, using an anonymous app user ID. We never see your payment details.
Some providers are based in the USA. Where data is transferred outside the EU, it is protected by the EU–US Data Privacy Framework or the EU Standard Contractual Clauses.

sections.heading: 6. How long we keep data
paragraphs: Your account, children's profiles, stories, pictures, coloring pages and book PDFs are kept until you delete them.

Deleting a story or a child removes it right away. Deleting your account (Settings → Delete my account) removes your account, children, stories, Books, PDFs, pictures and audio, and your sign-in account. You can also ask us to delete your account by email (see https://tallyapi-production-1103.up.railway.app/delete-account).
Story reports are kept for up to two years so we can review them and improve story safety; deleting your account removes the link to you.
Anonymous story scores and cost records without any content or link to you are kept to improve the service. Server logs and backups are deleted after a short period.

sections.heading: 7. Security
paragraphs: All connections are encrypted (HTTPS). Children's names are additionally encrypted in our database. Access to data is limited to what is needed to run the service.

sections.heading: 8. Your rights
paragraphs: You have the right to access your data, to correct it, to have it deleted, to restrict or object to its processing, and to receive it in a portable format. Most of this you can do directly in the app; for anything else, write to deneb.algedi2026@gmail.com.
You also have the right to complain to a data protection supervisory authority, for example the authority in the German federal state where you live.

sections.heading: 9. Children
paragraphs: Tally is used by parents on behalf of their children. Children should not create accounts themselves; settings, purchases and account deletion are behind a grown-ups check. If you believe a child has given us data without a parent, contact us and we will delete it.

sections.heading: 10. Changes
paragraphs: If we change this policy in an important way, we will tell you in the app. The current version is always at https://tallyapi-production-1103.up.railway.app/privacy.

samples.title: The Moth at the Star Window
paragraphs: The hilltop observatory looked like a little house wearing a round hat. Inside, a long telescope pointed towards a wide window. A lamp shone beside two chairs, and a tiny night-light glowed near the door.
“Welcome to our star window,” said Tansy, who looked after the observatory. “It’s where we look out at the sky.”
Emma hurried over, her notebook tucked beneath one arm.
“Will we see a planet?” she asked.
“A bright one, if the clouds leave us a gap.”
Tansy adjusted the telescope. Emma peered through it, but a pale reflection blurred her view.
“We’ll see better with the lamp turned down,” Tansy explained.
Emma glanced around. She liked the room just as it was. She could see every chair leg, every shelf, and both her shoes.
“Does it have to be very dark?” she asked.
“Not completely. Our little night-light can stay on.”
Still, Emma held her notebook closer. The corners beyond the lamp looked deep and unfamiliar.
Tansy sat beside her. “There’s no hurry.”
Outside, a thin cloud slid across the sky. Emma watched it pass and wished feeling brave could be as easy as waiting for a cloud.
Something flickered beside the lampshade.
At first, Emma thought it was a moving shadow. Then it settled, showing two soft brown wings.
“A moth,” she whispered.
It opened its wings and fluttered around the lamp again. Once around, twice around, then a wobbly loop beneath the shade.
“It seems to like our lamp more than our telescope,” said Tansy.
“Maybe it’s looking for a lamp planet.”
Tansy smiled. “A very bright one.”
But the moth kept circling. Emma watched its small wings beat against the warm glow.
“Shouldn’t it be outside?”
“Yes. Let’s give it a way out.”
Tansy opened the star window while Emma stayed beside the chairs. Cool air drifted in, carrying the smell of grass. Beyond the window lay the garden, silver-grey beneath the sky.
“There you are, little moth,” Tansy said gently.
The moth landed on the lampshade. It stayed there, nowhere near the opening.
“It hasn’t noticed,” said Emma.
“The lamp is very bright,” Tansy replied. “Turning it down may help.”
Emma looked from the lamp to the open window. She wanted to help. She also wanted every corner to stay bright.
“Will you stay right here?” Emma asked.
“Right beside you,” said Tansy. “And the night-light will stay on.”
Emma found its small golden glow near the door. Then she found the chair, the bookshelf, and Tansy’s cheerful face. Those things would still be there when the lamp grew dim.
She put her notebook on the chair.
“I think I can turn it down.”
Tansy showed her the lamp’s little dial. Emma rested her fingers on it and took a slow breath.
She turned it just a little.
The walls softened from yellow to grey. Nothing else changed. Her shoes were still beneath her. Tansy was still beside her.
“A little more?” Tansy asked.
Emma nodded and turned the dial again.
For a moment, the moth stayed still. Then its wings trembled open. It fluttered away from the shade, made one broad loop, and passed through the star window.
“There!” Emma whispered.
They watched it drift over the garden until it disappeared into the evening.
Emma let out her breath. She hadn’t noticed she was holding it.
“I felt worried,” she said. “But I did it.”
“You did,” said Tansy, staying close.
Tansy closed the star window gently, keeping the cool breeze outside. The night-light made a small golden patch across the floor.
Emma looked around. Now she could make out the bookshelf, the chairs, and her notebook without the bright lamp.
“The room hasn’t gone anywhere,” she said.
“No,” Tansy agreed. “And look—the clouds have moved.”
She checked the telescope, then stepped aside.
Emma leaned towards the eyepiece. There, against the dark sky, shone a bright, round planet.
“I found it!”
She looked for a long, quiet moment. The planet seemed wonderfully far away, while Tansy’s voice was comfortably close.
Before they finished, Emma drew a circle in her notebook. Beside it, she drew a moth with two wide wings.
“Two things to remember,” she said.
Later, tucked into bed in the observatory’s cozy guest room, she watched another small night-light glow beside the door. Tansy pulled the blanket gently over her feet.
“Goodnight, planet,” Emma murmured. “Goodnight, moth.”
She pictured the open sky and the soft brown wings. Then she rested her cheek against the pillow, warm and pleased, and let her eyes close.
samples.moral: Courage can be one small step, even when you feel unsure.

lesson.question: What helped Emma take her brave little step?
lesson.explanation: Emma felt worried, so she asked Tansy to stay close and kept the night-light on. She took her time and helped the moth, showing that you can feel unsure and still do something brave.

samples.title: Lena und der flatternde Sternenhimmel
paragraphs: Die kleine Sternwarte hatte ein rundes Dach wie eine umgedrehte Schüssel. Lena blieb davor stehen und schaute neugierig hinauf. Heute durfte sie mit ihrer Oma die Sterne besuchen.
„Haben die da oben genug Platz?“, fragte sie.
„Das sehen wir uns an“, sagte Oma lächelnd.
Drinnen standen weiche Sessel unter einer hohen Kuppeldecke. In der Mitte befand sich ein Gerät mit vielen kleinen Öffnungen.
„Das ist der Sternenprojektor“, erklärte Oma. „Er wirft Sterne und Planeten an die Decke.“
Lena setzte sich neben sie. Schon glitten helle Punkte über ihnen dahin. Dazwischen erschien ein großer Planet mit einem breiten Ring.
„Der trägt einen Hut!“, flüsterte Lena.
Oma schmunzelte. „Einen ziemlich flachen.“

Lena lehnte den Kopf zurück. Die Sterne funkelten wie winzige Löcher in einem dunkelblauen Tuch. Sie suchte nach Mustern und fand einen krummen Löffel. Daneben entdeckte sie etwas, das einem schlafenden Kaninchen ähnelte.
Am liebsten hätte sie jeden einzelnen Lichtpunkt gezählt. Doch immer, wenn sie bei zwölf angekommen war, entdeckte sie einen neuen.
Dann verschwanden die Sterne. Auch der Planet mit dem Hut war plötzlich fort. Der Sternenprojektor summte nicht mehr.
Lena setzte sich gerade hin. Ohne die Lichtpunkte wirkte die Kuppel auf einmal viel höher.
„Oma?“
„Ich bin hier.“ Sofort spürte sie Omas warme Hand.
Durch ein Fenster fiel ein wenig Abendlicht. Am Boden leuchteten kleine Lampen, die den Weg zeigten. Trotzdem zog Lena die Füße dicht an ihren Sessel.
„Die Vorstellung ist zu Ende“, sagte Oma ruhig. „Wir dürfen den Projektor noch einmal einschalten. Schau, der grüne Schalter ist gleich neben dir.“
An einer niedrigen Säule glomm ein grüner Punkt. Lena hätte ihn mit wenigen Schritten erreicht. Aber zwischen ihr und dem Schalter lag ein dunkles Stück Teppich.
Sie wollte aufstehen. Dann blieb sie doch sitzen.
„Im Dunkeln fühlt sich alles anders an“, murmelte sie.
„Ja“, sagte Oma. „Wir lassen uns Zeit. Ich bleibe bei dir.“
Lena drückte ihre Hand. Es tat gut, dass Oma nicht drängelte. Gemeinsam lauschten sie einen Augenblick in den stillen Raum.
Da huschte etwas am Fenster vorbei. Erst nach links, dann in einem Bogen zurück.
„Ein Blatt?“, fragte Lena.
Oma schaute hin. „Eine Fledermaus. Sie sucht draußen nach Insekten.“
Lena beugte sich neugierig vor. Vor dem hellen Abendhimmel erkannte sie zwei kleine Flügel. Die Fledermaus flatterte flink am Fenster entlang und drehte wieder um.
„Die fliegt ja lauter Kringel.“
„Dort schwirren kleine Mücken“, erklärte Oma. „Fledermäuse finden sich auch bei wenig Licht gut zurecht. Sie hören dabei besonders genau.“
Lena lauschte ebenfalls. Sie hörte Omas Atem und draußen das Rascheln der Blätter. Unter ihren Schuhen spürte sie den festen Teppich.
Der Raum war noch derselbe. Der Sessel war noch da. Oma auch.
„Ich möchte den Schalter drücken“, sagte sie. „Aber kommst du mit?“
„Natürlich.“
Sie standen zusammen auf. Lena hielt Omas Hand und machte einen Schritt. Dann noch einen. Jetzt konnte sie die niedrige Säule deutlich sehen.
Draußen zog die Fledermaus einen letzten kleinen Bogen vor dem Fenster.
Lena atmete langsam aus. Mit der freien Hand berührte sie den grünen Schalter und drückte ihn.
Ein leises Summen begann.
Über ihnen ging ein Stern an. Dann zehn. Dann so viele, dass Lena gar nicht erst zu zählen versuchte.
„Da ist mein Kaninchen wieder!“, sagte sie.
Oma setzte sich mit ihr in die weichen Sessel.
„Du hast dir Zeit genommen und es versucht“, sagte sie.
Lena nickte zufrieden. „Mit dir ging es leichter.“

Eine Weile betrachteten sie den ruhigen Himmel. Der Planet mit dem flachen Hut wanderte langsam über die Kuppel. Am Fenster war die Fledermaus nicht mehr zu sehen. Bestimmt suchte sie anderswo nach Mücken.
Später gingen Lena und Oma nach Hause. Über den Dächern standen nun echte Sterne. Sie bewegten sich nicht über eine Decke, sondern funkelten weit oben in der Nacht.
Im Bett kuschelte sich Lena unter ihre warme Decke. Oma blieb noch einen Moment bei ihr sitzen.
Lena dachte an die kleinen Flügel vor dem Fenster und an den grünen Schalter. Dann wurden ihre Augen schwer. Mit einem zufriedenen Seufzen schlief sie ein.
samples.moral: Mutig sein darf auch mit einer helfenden Hand beginnen.

lesson.question: Was hat Lena geholfen, sich im Dunkeln zum Schalter zu trauen?
lesson.explanation: Lena nahm sich Zeit und bat Oma, mitzukommen. Dann schaffte sie es, den Schalter zu drücken. Du darfst dir auch Hilfe holen, wenn du für etwas Mut brauchst.

samples.title: Les ailes sous les étoiles
paragraphs: Le soir descendait doucement sur le jardin. Les pâquerettes refermaient leurs pétales, et la menthe sentait bon. Sur la terrasse, Chloé attendait avec un gilet sur les épaules.
Mamie Praline est arrivée avec une lunette pour observer le ciel. Elle a déplié les trois pieds, puis posé l’appareil bien droit.

« Ce soir, nous allons chercher Saturne, a-t-elle annoncé.
— La planète avec des anneaux ?
— Oui. Mais pas des anneaux pour les doigts ! »
Chloé a ri. Elle imaginait une planète ouvrant une immense boîte à bijoux.
Au-dessus du pommier, un point brillait déjà. Mamie a orienté la lunette, tourné une petite molette, puis reculé d’un pas.
« Il faut encore patienter un peu. Le ciel devient plus sombre. »

Chloé a rapproché son petit tabouret. Elle aimait découvrir des choses, surtout celles qu’on ne remarquait pas au premier regard. Dans le jardin, elle connaissait les fourmis sous les pierres et les escargots derrière les pots.
Mais là-haut, tout semblait immense.

« Tu crois qu’on verra vraiment ses anneaux ?
— Regardons ensemble. Nous avons tout notre temps. »
À côté du tabouret, Mamie avait posé une couverture. La soirée pouvait commencer.
Chloé allait approcher son œil de la lunette quand une petite forme a traversé le ciel.
Une aile à gauche, une aile à droite, puis un brusque virage !
C’était une chauve-souris, un petit animal au corps couvert de poils, avec de fines ailes comme des voiles. Elle est passée près de la lunette avant de repartir vers le pommier.
Chloé a sursauté. Ses mains ont agrippé son gilet.

« Mamie ! Qu’est-ce que c’était ?
— Une chauve-souris qui cherche son dîner. »
Mais Chloé regardait déjà la porte de la maison. Les ailes lui avaient paru bien grandes. Et cette façon de tourner sans prévenir… Elle n’aimait pas ça du tout.
« Je veux rentrer. »
Mamie n’a pas ri. Elle s’est accroupie près d’elle.

« Tu as eu peur. Elle t’a surprise.
— On aurait dit qu’elle venait vers moi.
— Elle passait par ici. Nous pouvons nous asseoir un moment, si tu veux. »
Chloé a hésité. Elle voulait voir Saturne, mais ses jambes préféraient la cuisine.
Mamie lui a tendu la main, sans la presser.
La petite a posé sa main dans la sienne. Ensemble, elles se sont assises sur le banc, tout près de la terrasse.
Sur le banc, la couverture enveloppait les genoux de Chloé. Mamie restait contre elle. La porte de la maison était juste derrière.

« Regarde au-dessus du pommier, a murmuré Mamie. Tu vois les petits points qui bougent ?
— Les insectes ?
— Oui. La chauve-souris essaie de les attraper en vol. »
La petite silhouette a dessiné une boucle, puis une autre. Cette fois, Chloé l’a suivie des yeux.

« Pourquoi elle tourne autant ?
— Son dîner ne reste pas tranquillement dans une assiette. »
Chloé a laissé échapper un rire.
« Heureusement que mes petits pois ne volent pas ! »
Mamie a souri.
« Nous la regardons de loin, sans la toucher. Elle peut chercher ses insectes, et nous, notre planète. »
Chloé sentait encore un petit nœud dans son ventre. Pourtant, sur le banc, elle n’avait plus autant envie de partir.

« Je peux essayer de regarder dans la lunette… si tu restes à côté ?
— Bien sûr. Et tu peux faire une pause quand tu veux. »
Elles se sont levées doucement. Chloé a fait un pas, puis deux. Arrivée au tabouret, elle a soufflé lentement.
La chauve-souris tournait maintenant plus loin, au-dessus de la haie. Chloé a desserré les doigts et posé une main sur le bras de Mamie.
Mamie a vérifié la direction de la lunette. Puis Chloé a approché son œil.
D’abord, elle n’a vu qu’un rond sombre.
« Un tout petit peu plus haut », a soufflé Mamie.
Alors, une minuscule planète est apparue, pâle et lumineuse. Autour d’elle, ses anneaux formaient un délicat ovale.
« Oh… Elle est vraiment là ! »
Chloé ne bougeait presque plus. Saturne était bien plus petite que dans les livres, mais c’était Saturne, là, dans le ciel du jardin.
Elle a regardé longtemps, puis laissé sa place à Mamie.
Au-dessus de la haie, la chauve-souris est passée une dernière fois.
Chloé l’a remarquée sans reculer.
« Bon dîner », a-t-elle chuchoté.
Quand la fraîcheur est arrivée, elles ont replié la couverture. Mamie a rangé la lunette, et toutes deux sont rentrées.
Plus tard, bien au chaud dans son lit, Chloé a retrouvé Mamie pour un dernier câlin.

« J’avais encore un peu peur, mais j’ai vu les anneaux.
— Oui. Tu as pris ton temps. »
Mamie a remonté la couette sous son menton.
Derrière les rideaux, le jardin était tranquille. Chloé a fermé les yeux, avec une petite planète lumineuse dans ses pensées.
samples.moral: Être courageuse, c’est avancer doucement malgré sa peur, avec de l’aide si nécessaire.

lesson.question: Qu’est-ce qui a aidé Chloé à essayer de nouveau ?
lesson.explanation: Mamie a pris sa peur au sérieux et est restée près d’elle. Chloé a pris son temps pour observer la chauve-souris, puis regarder la planète. Tu peux aussi demander de l’aide et avancer à ton rythme.

samples.title: El observatorio de las orejas atentas
paragraphs: El observatorio del jardín tenía un techo redondo y una puerta azul. Dentro había un telescopio, dos bancos y una lámpara pequeña. Aquella noche, Lucía llegó con su tía Tita y una libreta para dibujar estrellas.
—Primero acomodamos todo —dijo Tita—. Después apagamos la lámpara para ver mejor el cielo.
Lucía dejó la libreta sobre un banco. Acomodó un cojín. Miró el telescopio. Luego miró la lámpara.
—¿Hay que apagarla del todo?
Tita se sentó a su lado.
—Su luz no nos deja distinguir las estrellas más pequeñas. Pero podemos esperar hasta que estés preparada.

A Lucía le encantaba imaginar planetas con jardines y lunas de colores. Sin embargo, cuando faltaba la luz, también imaginaba cosas detrás de cada sombra. La chaqueta colgada parecía tener unos brazos larguísimos.
—Esa chaqueta está haciendo de pulpo —murmuró.
Tita movió una manga y las dos rieron.
Después escucharon juntas. Sonó un grillo. Las hojas rozaron el techo. El banco crujió cuando Tita se acomodó.
—Esta noche tenemos un observatorio de orejas atentas —dijo ella.
Lucía sonrió, aunque todavía prefería la lámpara encendida. Acercó su cojín al de Tita y abrió la libreta por una página limpia.
Entonces entró una polilla, un pequeño insecto nocturno de alas suaves y pardas. Pasó por la puerta abierta y voló directamente hacia la lámpara.
Dio una vuelta. Luego otra. Su sombra recorrió la pared como un abanico diminuto.
—Creo que busca una estrella —dijo Lucía.
—La luz de aquí la ha atraído —explicó Tita—. Vamos a ayudarla a salir sin tocarle las alas.
Lucía señaló la puerta.
—Por aquí, polilla. El jardín es mucho más grande.
Pero la visitante siguió dando vueltas alrededor de la lámpara. Tita abrió un poco más la puerta y se apartó. Lucía hizo lo mismo al otro lado, dejando libre el camino.
Esperaron en silencio. La polilla se posó un instante en la pared, pero enseguida regresó a la luz.
—Nuestras indicaciones no le interesan mucho —dijo Lucía.
—Tal vez necesite que cambiemos algo, en lugar de explicárselo.
La niña miró la lámpara y comprendió. Si seguía encendida, la polilla querría quedarse cerca.
—Podríamos apagarla —propuso, en voz muy baja.
Al decirlo, notó un cosquilleo en la barriga. Buscó la mano de Tita, que estaba justo a su lado. La lámpara parecía muy pequeña; las sombras del observatorio, en cambio, le parecían enormes.
—¿Y si después no veo nada? —preguntó Lucía.
—Al principio veremos poco —respondió Tita—. Luego nuestros ojos se acostumbrarán. Yo estaré aquí, y podemos encenderla de nuevo cuando lo necesites.
Juntas comprobaron que no había nada en el suelo. Tita dejó la puerta bien abierta y volvió junto a ella. Desde allí se veía un trozo de jardín bajo la luz de la luna.
Lucía apoyó un dedo en el interruptor. Lo retiró una vez. Respiró despacio y volvió a colocarlo.
—¿Me das la mano?
—Claro.
Clic.
La lámpara se apagó.
Durante unos instantes, Lucía solo distinguió la puerta, un rectángulo algo más claro. Apretó la mano de Tita. Escuchó las hojas y reconoció al grillo de antes. Todo seguía en su sitio.
Pronto apareció el borde del banco. Después, el cojín. La chaqueta ya no parecía un pulpo: parecía una chaqueta descansando.
La polilla pasó cerca de ellas con un aleteo suave.
—Dejémosle espacio —susurró Tita.
Se apartaron juntas. Libre de la luz que la atraía, la polilla recorrió la pared, encontró la puerta y salió al jardín.
Lucía la vio cruzar el marco claro y perderse entre las plantas.
—Ya está fuera.
Su voz sonó contenta, pero bajita, como si no quisiera interrumpir la noche.
Tita acercó el banco al telescopio y ayudó a Lucía a mirar. En el círculo oscuro aparecieron varios puntos brillantes. La niña contuvo el aliento y luego sonrió.
—Estaban ahí todo el tiempo.
—Sí. Ahora podemos verlos mejor.
Lucía apartó un momento el ojo del telescopio. También a simple vista descubrió muchas estrellas sobre el techo redondo. Algunas brillaban con fuerza; otras apenas asomaban.
Ya no necesitó sujetar la mano de Tita, aunque le gustó tenerla cerca.
—Tuve miedo al apagarla —dijo—. Pero pude hacerlo contigo.
Tita le acarició el hombro.
Se quedaron un ratito más, mirando por turnos y escuchando el jardín. Después encendieron la lámpara para guardar la libreta y acomodar los cojines.
Regresaron a casa juntas por el sendero conocido. En su cama, Lucía recordó las alas pardas cruzando la puerta y los puntitos del cielo.

La oscuridad todavía le pareció grande, pero ya conocía algunas de las cosas que guardaba. Se arropó hasta los hombros. Tita le dio las buenas noches y permaneció cerca mientras la niña cerraba los ojos, despacito.
samples.moral: Ser valiente también es pedir compañía para intentar algo que nos da miedo.

lesson.question: ¿Qué ayudó a Lucía a atreverse a apagar la lámpara?
lesson.explanation: Lucía contó lo que sentía y pidió la mano de Tita. No necesitó dejar de sentir miedo para intentarlo: con compañía y sin prisas, ayudó a la polilla y descubrió las estrellas.

samples.title: Il pipistrello sotto le stelle
paragraphs: L'osservatorio sembrava una casetta con un cappello rotondo. Sorgeva sulla collina, dove le luci del paese arrivavano appena.
Giulia salì gli ultimi gradini tenendo la mano di zia Pina. Sopra di loro, il cielo diventava blu come una prugna.
«Qui si guardano le stelle», spiegò la zia. «Per questo si chiama osservatorio.»
Dentro c'erano due sgabelli, una carta del cielo e un telescopio. La cupola era aperta: tra i suoi bordi brillava già una stellina.
Giulia avrebbe voluto fare almeno cento domande. Il telescopio ingrandiva anche la Luna? Le stelle avevano tutte lo stesso colore?
Poi zia Pina indicò l'interruttore.
«Per vederle bene, dobbiamo spegnere la luce.»
La bambina strinse un poco la sua mano.
«Proprio tutta?»
«Tutta quella della stanza. Ma io resto qui.»
Giulia guardò gli angoli, la finestra e la lunga tenda raccolta accanto al muro. Con la lampada accesa, ogni cosa aveva un posto preciso. Al buio, chissà.
«Possiamo aspettare ancora un momento?» domandò.
«Certamente», rispose zia Pina. «Le stelle non hanno un treno da prendere.»
Giulia sorrise. Si sedette sullo sgabello, vicina alla zia, e guardò quella prima luce lontana.
Un fruscio leggerissimo passò vicino alla finestra aperta. Poi una piccola sagoma attraversò la stanza con due rapidi colpi d'ala.
Era un pipistrello, un piccolo mammifero dal pelo morbido, con grandi orecchie e ali sottili come ombrelli.
«Oh!» fece Giulia, ritraendo i piedi sotto lo sgabello.
«Restiamo tranquille e lasciamogli spazio», disse zia Pina.
Il pipistrello girò sotto la cupola, agile e guardingo.
«È piccolo come una briciola», sussurrò la bambina.
«Allora, per noi sarà Briciola.»
Proprio in quel momento, una corrente d'aria gonfiò la tenda. La stoffa scivolò davanti alla finestra, nascondendo l'apertura.
Briciola tornò verso il muro, poi cambiò direzione. Fece un altro giro, cercando una via libera.
«Non trova più l'apertura da cui è entrato», disse Giulia.
Zia Pina annuì e spense la lampada. La bambina le cercò subito la mano.
«Sono qui. Lo lasceremo tranquillo e gli daremo un'uscita libera.»
Nel buio si sentiva soltanto il lieve fruscio delle ali.
«Come fa a non urtare tutto?» chiese Giulia.
«Lancia piccoli richiami, così acuti che noi non li sentiamo. Ascolta l'eco che torna indietro e capisce dove sono gli ostacoli.»
Giulia tese l'orecchio. Non udì i richiami, ma immaginò Briciola in ascolto delle risposte della stanza.
La tenda ondeggiava appena. La sua estremità era vicina, a pochi passi dagli sgabelli.
Giulia guardò quel pezzo di buio e sentì la pancia stringersi. Avrebbe preferito riaccendere subito la lampada.
«Possiamo aprire noi la strada?» domandò piano.
«Sì. Basta raccogliere la tenda di lato. Vengo con te.»
La bambina scese dallo sgabello. Zia Pina le rimase accanto, senza lasciarle la mano.
Prima fecero un respiro lento. Poi un altro.
Piano piano, Giulia cominciò a distinguere il bordo del tavolo. La cupola non era sparita. Nemmeno la finestra. La luce delle stelle disegnava sul pavimento una macchia pallida.
«Adesso vedo un pochino», sussurrò.
«I tuoi occhi si stanno abituando», rispose la zia.
Camminarono insieme fino alla tenda, lontane dal passaggio di Briciola. Con entrambi i piedi sul pavimento, Giulia afferrò il bordo della stoffa. Era morbido e fresco tra le dita.
Per un momento esitò ancora. Poi lo tirò lentamente verso il muro, mentre zia Pina fissava la tenda al suo gancio.
La finestra tornò libera.
Le due si allontanarono e rimasero immobili. Nessuna mano cercò di prendere il pipistrello.
Briciola compì un giro, si avvicinò all'apertura e passò fuori con un battito leggero.
Giulia lo vide per un istante contro il cielo.
«Buonanotte, Briciola», disse, con un sorriso che la zia intuì anche al buio.
Rimasero accanto alla finestra ancora un momento. Fuori, l'aria sapeva di erba e di sera.
«Avevo paura», confessò Giulia.
«Lo so», rispose zia Pina. «E hai trovato il modo di aiutare Briciola, insieme a me.»
La bambina tornò allo sgabello. Il buio non era diventato il suo gioco preferito, ma adesso le sembrava meno sconosciuto.
Zia Pina sistemò il telescopio e la invitò a guardare. Nell'oculare comparvero tanti puntini luminosi, alcuni vicini, altri sparsi come semi.
«Sembrano briciole anche queste», disse Giulia.
«Briciole di luce», rispose la zia.
Osservarono una stella chiara e un piccolo gruppo che ricordava una tazzina. Poi guardarono il cielo senza telescopio, in silenzio. Non serviva dare un nome a tutto.
Quando arrivò il primo sbadiglio, zia Pina riaccese la lampada. La stanza tornò familiare: il tavolo, gli sgabelli, la tenda ben raccolta.
Tornarono a casa insieme, sotto lo stesso cielo.
Più tardi, nel suo letto, Giulia ripensò al fruscio delle ali e alla mano della zia. Fece un respiro lento, poi un altro.
Fuori brillavano le stelle. Il cuscino era fresco, la coperta morbida.
Con quel ricordo quieto, chiuse gli occhi.
samples.moral: Il coraggio può essere un piccolo passo, con qualcuno accanto.

lesson.question: Che cosa ha aiutato Giulia a essere coraggiosa?
lesson.explanation: Giulia aveva paura del buio, ma ha respirato piano ed è rimasta accanto alla zia. Con il suo aiuto ha liberato l'uscita per Briciola: essere coraggiosi non significa fare tutto da soli.

samples.title: De vleermuis tussen de sterren
paragraphs: De sterrenkoepel had een rond dak, net een omgekeerde kom. Noor stapte met haar moeder naar binnen. Het was er warm. Langs de stoelen brandden kleine, gele lampjes.
‘Straks gaan we planeten bekijken,’ zei haar moeder.
Noor knikte. Ze wilde vooral Saturnus zien. Die had ringen, alsof iemand een hoepel om zijn buik had geschoven.
Midden in de zaal stond de sterrenprojector. Het apparaat had ronde lenzen die alle kanten op wezen. Daarmee kon het sterren op het koepeldak laten verschijnen.
‘Het lijkt wel een kever met heel veel ogen,’ fluisterde Noor.
Haar moeder glimlachte. ‘Een kever die sterren strooit.’
Ze kozen twee stoelen naast het grote raam. Buiten kleurde de avondlucht zachtblauw. Een struik bewoog een beetje in de wind.
Noor zette haar voeten op het voetenbankje. Ze keek van de projector naar het dak. Daar was nog geen ster te zien.
‘Moeten we lang wachten?’ vroeg ze.
‘Niet lang. Eerst wordt het licht zachter. Dan kunnen we alles goed zien.’
Noor leunde achterover. Ze was klaar voor de ringen van Saturnus.
De projector zoemde. Boven hun hoofden verscheen een eerste wit stipje. Daarna kwamen er tien, twintig, zoveel dat Noor niet meer kon tellen.
Tegelijk werden de gele lampjes zwakker.
De stoelen verloren hun kleur. De rand van het dak verdween. Opeens leek de koepel veel groter dan daarnet.
Noor ging rechtop zitten. Haar vingers zochten de hand van haar moeder. Die was gelukkig vlakbij.
Er schoof een grote, ronde planeet over het dak. Maar Noor keek niet meer naar boven. Ze keek naar het lampje naast haar stoel. Het gaf nog maar een dun streepje licht.
‘Mag het licht weer aan?’ vroeg ze snel.
‘Natuurlijk,’ zei haar moeder.
Ze drukte op het knopje naast de stoel. De lampjes werden weer helder. Meteen zag Noor de rijen stoelen en haar eigen schoenen.
Ze blies langzaam haar adem uit.
‘Ik wilde de planeten zo graag zien,’ zei ze. ‘Maar dit donker vind ik niet fijn.’
‘We hoeven ons niet te haasten,’ antwoordde haar moeder. ‘Ik blijf naast je.’
Even zaten ze stil. De projector zoemde zachtjes verder, zonder dat iemand iets hoefde te zeggen.
Toen bewoog er iets achter het raam.
Noor draaide haar hoofd. Buiten scheerde een klein dier langs de struik. Het had brede vleugels en maakte een snelle bocht.
‘Een vleermuis,’ zei haar moeder zacht.
De vleermuis fladderde terug. Boven de struik dansten piepkleine insecten. Hap! Er verdween er eentje.
‘Is die aan het eten?’ vroeg Noor.
‘Ja. Een avondmaaltijd in de lucht.’
Noor moest lachen. ‘Zonder tafel?’
‘En zonder bord.’
Ze keek hoe de vleermuis nog een rondje maakte. Buiten werd de lucht steeds donkerder. Toch vloog het dier rustig verder, heen en terug langs de struik.
‘Een vleermuis maakt heel hoge geluidjes,’ vertelde haar moeder. ‘Aan de echo hoort die waar iets is. Ook waar een insect vliegt.’
Noor luisterde. Ze hoorde alleen het zachte zoemen van de projector.
‘Die geluidjes zijn te hoog voor onze oren,’ zei haar moeder.
Een poosje keek Noor naar buiten. Daarna keek ze naar de lampjes binnen.
‘Mag het licht een klein beetje zachter?’ vroeg ze. ‘Niet meteen helemaal.’
Haar moeder draaide aan het knopje.
Eén stapje donkerder. Noor voelde de vertrouwde hand naast zich. Ze keek omhoog. Er verschenen alweer drie sterren.
‘Nog een klein beetje,’ zei Noor na een tijdje.
Het licht werd zachter. Boven haar hoofd kwamen steeds meer sterren tevoorschijn. Eerst waren het losse stipjes. Nu zag ze een hele strook die glinsterde als fijn zand.
Haar moeder bleef naast haar zitten. Ze hoefde niet verder aan het knopje te draaien dan Noor prettig vond.
Toen verscheen Saturnus.
‘Daar is de planeet met de hoepel!’ fluisterde Noor.
De ringen waren breed en licht. Ze keek er zo aandachtig naar dat ze haar voetenbankje even vergat.
Het donker was er nog. Maar haar moeder was er ook. En nu kon ze de sterren zien waarvoor ze was gekomen.
‘Ik heb zelf gevraagd of het zachter mocht,’ zei ze.
‘Ja,’ antwoordde haar moeder. ‘Steeds een stapje.’
Noor glimlachte trots en legde haar hoofd tegen haar moeders arm.
Buiten fladderde de vleermuis nog eenmaal langs het raam. Binnen schoof Saturnus langzaam verder over het ronde dak.
Niemand hoefde ergens heen. Noor keek nog even omhoog, met zware oogleden en een rustig gevoel. De sterren glansden zacht boven haar.
samples.moral: Dapper zijn mag stapje voor stapje, met iemand naast je.

lesson.question: Wat hielp Noor om naar de sterren te durven kijken?
lesson.explanation: Noor vertelde wat ze spannend vond en vroeg om hulp. Ze liet het licht in kleine stapjes zachter zetten, terwijl haar moeder naast haar bleef. Je mag rustig de tijd nemen als iets nieuw of spannend is.

samples.title: כוכבים בקצה הזנב
paragraphs: בכניסה לפלנטריום, נועה עצרה והביטה בתמונה של כוכב לכת מוקף טבעות.
"גם אותו נראה?" שאלה את אמה.
"בואי נגלה," אמרה אמא, ולחצה בעדינות את ידה.
הפלנטריום היה אולם עם תקרה עגולה, ועליה הקרינו את שמי הלילה. היו בו כורסאות רכות, ומנורות קטנות האירו את המעבר. התקרה נראתה כמו קערה ענקית הפוכה מעל הראש.
תותי, המדריכה, חיכתה ליד הכורסאות. לצדה ישב פופקורן, הכלב שלה, שנועה כבר הכירה מביקור קודם. הוא כשכש בזנבו, אבל נשאר במקומו, רגוע כהרגלו.
"ברוכה הבאה," אמרה תותי. "היום נטייל בין כוכבי לכת בלי לקום מהכורסה."
"אז לא צריך לארוז כריכים?" שאלה נועה.
תותי צחקה. "רק להביא עיניים סקרניות."
נועה בחרה כורסה ליד אמא. היא הניחה את ידיה על המשענות והביטה למעלה. על התקרה הופיע עיגול כחול קטן.
"כדור הארץ," הסבירה תותי. "ממנו נתחיל. בקרוב אחליש את האור, כדי שנראה היטב את הכוכבים."
נועה הנהנה. היא רצתה מאוד לראות אותם, ונשענה לאחור כדי לא להחמיץ דבר.
האור נחלש מעט. הכורסאות האפירו, ופינות האולם היטשטשו.
נועה הזדקפה מיד.
"רגע," אמרה. "אפשר לעצור? אני לא רוצה שיהיה חושך עכשיו."
תותי עצרה את העמעום. מנורות המעבר המשיכו להאיר, ואור רך נשאר מעל הכורסאות.
"בוודאי," אמרה. "נישאר ככה. אין שום צורך למהר."
אמא הושיטה יד, ונועה אחזה בה. היא עדיין ראתה את פניה של אמא, את הדלת ואת השטיח שמתחת לרגליה. ובכל זאת, הבטן שלה התכווצה קצת.
ליד תותי, פופקורן קם וניגש לשמיכה שלו. הוא רחרח קצה אחד, רחרח את הקצה השני, ואז הסתובב עליה סיבוב שלם. לבסוף נשכב באנחה ארוכה, כאילו סיים לסדר אולם שלם לבדו.
נועה פלטה צחוק קטן.
"הוא בודק שזאת המיטה הנכונה?"
"כנראה," אמרה תותי. "הוא בררן מאוד בענייני שמיכות."
פופקורן הניח את הסנטר על כפותיו. אוזן אחת שלו נשארה מקופלת, והוא אפילו לא טרח ליישר אותה.
נועה הביטה בו. הוא הכיר את האולם היטב, ובאור הרך רק חיפש תנוחה נוחה. היא שחררה מעט את אחיזתה ביד של אמא.
"אפשר ללטף אותו?" שאלה נועה את תותי.
"כן, בעדינות, על הגב. הוא אוהב את זה."
פופקורן נח קרוב לכורסה שלה. נועה הושיטה יד וליטפה את פרוותו החמימה. הוא הרים אליה מבט, כשכש פעם אחת, והניח שוב את ראשו.
היא נשמה לאט. אמא נשארה לצדה, ותותי חיכתה בלי לגעת במתג.
כעבור רגע אמרה נועה, "אולי אפשר להחליש בכל פעם רק קצת? ואז לחכות שאסתכל מסביב?"
"רעיון טוב," אמרה תותי. "ואת יכולה לבקש לעצור בכל שלב."
האור נחלש מעט. נועה ראתה את אמא, את פס האור במעבר ואת השמיכה של פופקורן.
"ככה בסדר," אמרה אחרי רגע.
תותי חיכתה עד שנועה הנהנה, ורק אז עמעמה עוד קצת. הפעם נצצו על התקרה הרבה נקודות קטנות. האולם נשאר חשוך למחצה, אבל עכשיו התמונה נראתה ברורה יותר.
"אני רוצה להישאר," אמרה נועה. היא הרגישה עוד דגדוג קטן של חשש, אבל כבר לא רצתה להביט רק במנורות.
כוכב לכת זהוב הופיע מעליהן, וסביבו טבעות רחבות.
"שבתאי!" היא הצביעה בהתרגשות. "זה שבתמונה בכניסה!"
"נכון מאוד," אמרה תותי.
נועה עקבה בעיניה אחרי הטבעות. היה נדמה לה ששבתאי חבש כובע גדול, והיא חייכה אל אמא.
בהמשך הופיע על התקרה פס אור עדין, מלא נקודות צפופות.
"זה שביל החלב," אמרה תותי בשקט. "פס האור הזה מורכב מהמוני כוכבים רחוקים."
נועה הביטה בו זמן ארוך. היו בו אזורים בהירים ואזורים עמומים, כמו ענן שאפשר לראות בתוכו עוד ועוד אורות.
"אמא," לחשה, "אני עדיין קצת חוששת. אבל גם נעים לי כאן."
אמא ליטפה את ידה. "שני הדברים יכולים להיות יחד. ואני כאן איתך."
פופקורן התמתח על השמיכה והתכרבל לרגליהן. קצה זנבו נח קרוב לפס האור שעל הרצפה.
"אפילו הזנב שלו כמעט מגיע לכוכבים," לחשה נועה.
אמא חייכה, והשתיים נשענו זו על זו.

כשההקרנה הסתיימה, תותי החזירה את האור בהדרגה. הכוכבים נעלמו לאט, והכורסאות חזרו לצבען המוכר. נועה לא מיהרה לקום. היא הקשיבה לנשימותיו השקטות של פופקורן ונחה עוד רגע ליד אמא, חמימה ונינוחה, ובראשה עדיין הסתובבו הטבעות של שבתאי.
samples.moral: אפשר להיות אמיצים גם כשקצת חוששים, ולבקש להתקדם לאט.

lesson.question: מה עזר לנועה להישאר וליהנות מהכוכבים?
lesson.explanation: נועה סיפרה שהיא חוששת וביקשה להחליש את האור לאט. היא נעזרה באמא, בתותי ובפופקורן, ובחרה להמשיך בקצב שהתאים לה. אומץ לא מחייב שהחשש ייעלם לגמרי.
